source_text: Ὡς οὖν ἀπὸ Ἀβραὰμ ἤρξατο περιτομὴ καὶ ἀπὸ Μωσέως σάββατον καὶ θυσίαι καὶ προσφοραὶ καὶ ἑορταὶ, καὶ ἀπεδείχθη διὰ τὸ σκληροκάρδιον τοῦ λαοῦ ὑμῶν ταῦτα διατετάχθαι, οὕτως παύσασθαι ἔδει κατὰ τὴν τοῦ πατρὸς βουλὴν εἰς τὸν διὰ τῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ γένους τοῦ Ἀδραὰμ καὶ φυλῆς Ἰούδα καὶ Δαυῒδ παρθένου γεννηθέντα υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ Χριστόν, ὅστις καὶ αἰώνιος νόμος καὶ καινὴ διαθήκη τῷ παντὶ κόσμῳ ἐκηρύσσετο προελευσόμενος, ὡς αἱ προλελεγμέναι προφητεῖαι σημαίνουσι. Καὶ ἡμεῖς, οἱ διὰ τούτου προσχωρήσαντες τῷ θεῷ, οὐ ταύτην τὴν κατὰ σάρκα παρελάβομεν περιτομήν, ἀλλὰ πνευματικήν , ἣν Ἐνὼχ καὶ οἱ ὅμοιοι ἐφύλαξαν· ἡμεῖς δὲ διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος αὐτήν, ἐπειδὴ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἐγεγόνειμεν, διὰ τὸ ἔλεος τὸ παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐλάβομεν, καὶ πᾶσιν ἐφετὸν ὁμοίως λαμβάνειν. Περὶ δὲ τοῦ τῆς γενέσεως αὐτοῦ μυστηρίου ἤδη λέγειν κατεπείγοντος λέγω. Ἡσαΐας οὖν περὶ τοῦ γένους αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅτι ἀνεκδιήγητόν ἐστιν ἀνθρώποις, οὕτως ἔφη ὡς καὶ προγέγραπται· Τὴν γενεὰν αὐτοῦ τίς διηγήσεται; Ὅτι αἴρεται ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ, ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνομιῶν τοῦ λαοῦ μου ἤχθη εἰς θάνατον . Ὡς ἀνεκδιηγήτου οὖν ὄντος τοῦ γένους τούτου ἀποθνήσκειν μέλλοντος, ἵνα τῷ μώλωπι αὐτοῦ ἰαθῶμεν οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἄνθρωποι, τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα ταῦτα εἶπεν. Ἔτι καὶ ἵνα ὃν τρόπον γέγονεν ἐν κόσμῳ γεννηθεὶς ἐπιγνῶναι ἔχωσιν οἱ πιστεύοντες αὐτῷ ἄνθρωποι, διὰ τοϋ αὐτοῦ Ἡσαίου τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα ὡς μέλλει γίνεσθαι προεφήτευσεν οὕτως· Καὶ προσέθετο κύριος λαλῆσαι τῷ Ἄχαζ, λέγων· Αἴτησον σεαυτῷ σημεῖον παρὰ κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ σου εἰς βάθος ἢ εἰς ὕψος. Καὶ εἶπεν Ἄχαζ· Οὐ μὴ αἰτήσω οὐδ᾿ οὐ μὴ πειράσω κύριον. Καὶ εἶπεν Ἡσαίας· Ἀκούετε δή, οἶκος Δαυΐδ. Μὴ μικρὸν ὑμῖν ἀγῶνα παρέχειν ἀνθρώποις; Καὶ πῶς κυρίῳ παρέχετε ἀγῶνα; Διὰ τοῦτο δώσει κύριος αὐτὸς ὑμῖν σημεῖον· ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ λήψεται καὶ τέξεται υἱόν, καὶ καλέσεται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἐμμανουήλ. Βούτυρον καὶ μέλι φάγεται. Πρὶν ἢ γνῶναι αὐτὸν ἢ προελέσθαι πονηρὰ ἐκλέξεται τὸ ἀγαθόν· διότι, πρὶν ἢ γνῶναι τὸ παιδίον ἀγαθὸν ἢ κακόν. ἀπειθεῖ πονηρὰ τοῦ ἐκλέξασθαι τὸ ἀγαθόν. Διότι, πρὶν ἢ γνῶναι τὸ παιδίον καλεῖν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα, λήψεται δύναμιν Δαμασκοῦ καὶ σκύλα Σαμαρείας ἔναντι βασιλέως Ἀσσυρίων. Καὶ καταληφθήσεται ἡ γῆ, ἣν σὺ σκληρῶς οἴσεις ἀπὸ προσώπου τῶν δύο βασιλέων. Ἀλλ᾿ ἐπάξει ὁ θεὸς ἐπὶ σὲ καἰ ἐπὶ τὸν λαόν σου καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον τοῦ πατρός σου ἡμέρας. αἳ οὐδέπω ἥκασιν ἐπὶ σέ, ἀπὸ τῆς ἡμέρας ᾗς ἀφεῖλεν Ἐφραῒμ ἀπὸ Ἰούδα τὸν βασιλέα τῶν Ἀσσυρίων [Is., XVII. 10-16a; VIII, 4; VII, 16 b-17]. Ὅτι μὲν οὖν ἐν τῷ γένει τῷ κατὰ σάρκα τοῦ Ἀβραὰμ οὐδεὶς ουδέποτε ἀπὸ παρθένου γεγέννηται οὐδὲ λέλεκται γεγεννημένος ἀλλ᾿ ἢ οὗτος ὁ ἡμέτερος Χριστός, πᾶσι φανερόν ἐστιν. Ἐπεὶ δὲ ὑμεῖς καὶ οἱ διδάσκαλοι ὑμῶν τολμᾶτε λέγειν μηδὲ εἰρῆσθαι ἐν τῇ προφητείᾳ τοῦ Ἡσαΐου Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει, ἀλλ᾿ Ἰδοὺ ἡ νεᾶνις ἐν γαστρὶ λήψεται καὶ τέξεται υἱόν, καὶ ἐξηγεῖσθε τὴν προφητείαν ὡς εἰς Ἐζεκίαν, τὸν γενόμενον ὑμῶν βασιλέα, πειράσομαι καὶ ἐν τούτῳ καθ᾿ ὑμῶν βραχέα ἐξηγήσασθαι καὶ ἀποδεῖξαι εἰς τοῦτον εἰρῆσθαι τὸν ὁμολογούμενον ὑφ᾿ ἡμῶν Χριστόν.
pass_a_gloss: So then circumcision began from Abraham and the Sabbath and sacrifices and offerings and festivals from Moses, and it was shown because of the hardness of heart of your people that these things were commanded, thus it was necessary for them to cease according to the plan of the Father for the Son of God Christ who was born from the genus of Adam and the tribe of Judah and David through a virgin, who is also the eternal law and the new covenant that was proclaimed to the whole world, as the prophecies that were spoken beforehand signify. And we who have come to God through Him did not receive this circumcision according to the flesh, but a spiritual one, which Enoch and those like him kept; we however received it through baptism, since we had become sinners, through the mercy that is from God, and it is available for all to receive equally. Now, concerning the mystery of His birth, I must speak. Isaiah spoke about the genus of Christ, that it is unspeakable to men, and he said as it is written: 'Who will declare His genus?' For His life is taken away from the earth, He was led to death because of the iniquities of my people. Since the genus of this one who is about to die is unspeakable, the prophetic Spirit said these things so that we sinners may be healed by His wound. And also so that believers in Him may know how He came into the world, the prophetic Spirit prophesied through Isaiah beforehand as follows: And the Lord added to speak to Ahaz, saying, 'Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your God, either in depth or in height.' And Ahaz said, 'I will not ask, nor will I test the Lord.' And Isaiah said, 'Hear, O house of David, will you give little trouble to men? And how do you give trouble to the Lord?' Therefore, the Lord Himself will give you a sign: behold, the virgin will have in her womb and will bear a son, and she will call His name Emmanuel. He will eat butter and honey. Before He knows or chooses good or evil, He will choose the good; for before the child knows good or evil, He will choose the good. For before the child knows how to call father or mother, He will take hold of the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria in the presence of the king of Assyria. And the land which you will painfully possess will be taken away from the presence of the two kings. But God will bring upon you and upon your people and upon the house of your father days that have not yet come upon you, from the day on which Ephraim turned away from Judah the king of the Assyrians. For it is clear to all that in the fleshly genus of Abraham no one has ever been born of a virgin, nor has it been said that anyone was born, except this our Christ. Since you and your teachers dare to say that it is not said in the prophecy of Isaiah, 'Behold, the virgin will have in her womb and will bear a son,' but rather 'Behold, the young woman will have in her womb and will bear a son,' and you interpret the prophecy as referring to Hezekiah, your king, I will try to explain briefly and demonstrate that it refers to the Christ who is confessed by us.

pass_b_english: Circumcision began with Abraham; the Sabbath, sacrifices, offerings, and festivals began with Moses. These things were commanded because your people were hard of heart, and they had to cease according to the Father's plan for the Son of God, Christ, who was born from the line of Adam and the tribe of Judah and David through a virgin. He is also the eternal law and the new covenant proclaimed to the whole world, as the earlier prophecies signify. We who have drawn near to God through Him did not receive circumcision according to the flesh, but a spiritual one, which Enoch and those like him kept. We, however, received it through baptism because we had become sinners, through the mercy from God, and it is available for all to receive equally.

Now I must speak about the mystery of His birth. Isaiah said concerning the line of Christ that it is unspeakable to men: 'Who will declare His generation? For His life is taken away from the earth, He was led to death because of the iniquities of my people' (Isaiah 53:8). Since the line of this One who was about to die is unspeakable, the prophetic Spirit spoke these things so that we sinners might be healed by His wound. And also so that believing humans might know how He came into the world, the prophetic Spirit prophesied beforehand through Isaiah as follows: 'And the Lord spoke again to Ahaz, saying, Ask a sign for yourself from the Lord your God, in the depth or in the height. And Ahaz said, I will not ask, nor will I test the Lord. And Isaiah said, Hear then, O house of David. Is it too little for you to weary men? And how do you weary the Lord? Therefore the Lord Himself will give you a sign: Behold, the virgin will have in her womb and will bear a son, and she will call His name Emmanuel. He will eat butter and honey. Before He knows or chooses evil, He will choose the good; for before the child knows good or evil, He will choose the good. For before the child knows how to call father or mother, He will take the power of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria before the king of Assyria. And the land that you painfully possess will be taken away from before the two kings. But God will bring upon you and upon your people and upon the house of your father days that have not yet come upon you, from the day on which Ephraim turned away from Judah the king of the Assyrians.'

For it is clear to all that in the fleshly line of Abraham no one has ever been born of a virgin, nor has it been said that anyone was born, except this our Christ. Since you and your teachers dare to say that it is not said in the prophecy of Isaiah, 'Behold, the virgin will have in her womb and will bear a son, and she will call His name Emmanuel' (Isaiah 7:14), but rather 'Behold, the young woman will have in her womb and will bear a son,' and you interpret the prophecy as referring to Hezekiah, your king, I will try to explain briefly and demonstrate against you that it refers to the Christ we confess.
